value.body: A two-year master's in one area of fisheries science, such as aquaculture, fish processing technology, fisheries resource management, aquatic animal health, fish nutrition, fish genetics or fisheries extension. It combines coursework with a research thesis, and leads to research, technical and scientist roles.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.F.Sc (some specialisations also accept related science graduates). Admission is through ICAR's all-India PG entrance (AICE-JRF/SRF), which also awards fellowships, or the university's own entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Offered by state fisheries, veterinary and agricultural universities and ICAR's deemed university for fisheries.
A master's is required for the ICAR scientist exam (ARS) and is usual for research posts.
Many graduates go on to a PhD with an ICAR or university fellowship.

value.title: Students enrolled in M.F.Sc.
value.note: Part of the rise from 2021-22 may reflect more institutions responding rather than more students. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, M.F.Sc. -Master of Fishery Science), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
